facts.statement: The genus Ischioceratops was named and described in 2015 by a team of seven researchers including He Yiming and Xu Xing.
facts.quote: In 2015, the type species Ischioceratops zhuchengensis was named and described by He Yiming, Peter J. Makovicky, Wang Kebai, Chen Shuqing, Corwin Sullivan, Han Fenglu and Xu Xing.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Ischioceratops was discovered in Kugou, Shandong Province, China.
facts.quote: The holotype ZCDM V0O016 was discovered in Kugou, a locality in the Shandong Province of China

facts.statement: Ischioceratops lived approximately 77.3 to 73.5 million years ago in what is now China.
facts.quote: Ischioceratops () is an extinct genus of small herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur that lived approximately 77.3-73.5 million years ago during the latter part of the Cretaceous Period in what is now China.

facts.statement: Ischioceratops was a small, quadrupedal herbivore estimated to reach a total length of about 2 meters.
facts.quote: Ischioceratops was a small sized, moderately-built, ground-dwelling, quadrupedal herbivore, whose total body length has been estimated to be about 2 m.

facts.statement: The name Ischioceratops means "ischium horned face" and refers to the unique shape of its ischium bones.
facts.quote: Its name means "ischium horned face", referring to the peculiar shape of the ischiatic bones.

facts.statement: The ischium of Ischioceratops has a robust shaft resembling a recurved bow that flares into a subrectangular obturator process with an elliptical hole.
facts.quote: the ischium has a robust shaft that resembles that of a recurved bow and flares gradually to form a subrectangular-shaped obturator process in its middle portion while an elliptical fenestra perforates the obturator process.

facts.statement: The unique shape of the ischium in Ischioceratops is considered a single autapomorphy unique to all dinosaurs.
facts.quote: This morphology, unique for the Dinosauria as a whole, was seen as a single autapomorphy, unique derived character.

facts.statement: Ischioceratops is one of the few known ceratopsian dinosaurs for which no skull fossils have been found.
facts.quote: Ischioceratops is one of the few ceratopsian dinosaurs which is not known by the skull.

facts.statement: Ischioceratops possessed an elevation on the proximal part of its tail that formed a tail crest, a feature also seen in other ceratopsians.
facts.quote: Another characteristic of Ischioceratops is the presence of an elevation in the proximal part of its tail, which is present also in Protoceratops, Koreaceratops and in a more similar way in Montanoceratops and Cerasinops. The elevation forms a tail crest.

facts.statement: Ischioceratops is classified within the family Leptoceratopsidae and is distinguished by having nine sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: The taxon has been referred to Leptoceratopsidae and is distinguished from other known leptoceratopsids based on the following combination of characters: nine sacral vertebrae, more than in any other known basal (non-ceratopsid) ceratopsian but fewer than in ceratopsids

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis confirms Ischioceratops as a leptoceratopsid with Montanoceratops as its closest relative.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analyzes confirmed Ischioceratops as a leptoceratopsid. Its closest relative taxon or sister species was Montanoceratops.

facts.statement: Ischioceratops lived in the Wangshi Group during the late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Ischioceratops existed in the Wangshi Group during the late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Ischioceratops lived alongside centrosaurines, saurolophines, and tyrannosaurines.
facts.quote: It lived alongside centrosaurines, saurolophines, and tyrannosaurines.

facts.statement: Ischioceratops belongs to the family Leptoceratopsidae.
The time range for Ischioceratops is recorded as the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The generic name combines a reference to the uniquely formed ischium with the suffix "ceratops," meaning "horn face."
rejected.quote: The generic name combines a reference to the os ischii, its uniquely formed ischium, with ~ceratops, "horn face", a usual suffix in the names of Ceratopia.
